title: Timeouts, Retries, and Failure Policies knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly describes Timeouts, Retries, and Failure Policies?
options: Run untrusted pull-request code in the same job that holds production credentials.
Set timeouts and bounded retry logic for transient failures; do not retry deterministic test or configuration errors indefinitely or silently accept them.
Give every job write permission to avoid troubleshooting authorization errors.
Print all environment variables and event payloads to make the run easier to debug.
questions.answer_key: Set timeouts and bounded retry logic for transient failures; do not retry deterministic test or configuration errors indefinitely or silently accept them.
questions.explanation: This is the central behavior of timeouts, retries, and failure policies: Set timeouts and bounded retry logic for transient failures; do not retry deterministic test or configuration errors indefinitely or silently accept them. Validate configuration and behavior against the current official reference before production use.

Measure duration, resource/runner consumption, queue time, and failure rate before changing the pipeline. Bound retries, cancel stale work only when safe, and compare the result after one controlled change.

questions.prompt: How should a reviewer verify a change related to timeouts, retries, and failure policies?
options: Publish the workflow to production before reviewing its triggers and permissions.
Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
Assume the workflow is correct as soon as the YAML file is committed.
Retry every failure without looking at the exit code or preserving evidence.
questions.answer_key: Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
questions.explanation: Reliable verification uses observable evidence. For this lesson, consider: Set timeouts and bounded retry logic for transient failures; do not retry deterministic test or configuration errors indefinitely or silently accept them. A syntax check alone cannot prove remote execution, permissions, or deployment behavior.
